title: Extremal torus weights give affine projective attraction charts
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], let $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ be a split torus [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sc-gm-ga], and let $E\ne0$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] with a rational $T$-representation, meaning a group-scheme homomorphism $T\to\operatorname{GL}(E)$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Let $X$ be a nonempty smooth connected projective $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-pc-projective-morphism], with a $T$-equivariant closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(E)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $\mathbf P(E)$ is projective space parametrizing lines [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Assume that the lines $i(x)$, for $x\in X(k)$, linearly span $E$, and that the fixed subscheme $X^T$ is a finite nonempty disjoint union of reduced $k$-points. Here $X^T$ represents points fixed by the action after every algebra extension. Write $E=\bigoplus_{\chi\in\Omega}E_\chi$ for its decomposition into nonzero character eigenspaces, where $\chi:T\to\mathbf G_m$ is a group-scheme homomorphism and $T$ acts on $E_\chi$ by scalar $\chi$. There exists a cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to T$ such that the integers $m_\chi$ given by $\chi(\lambda(t))=t^{m_\chi}$ are pairwise distinct. For every such $\lambda$, let $\chi_0$ be the unique character of least $m_\chi$. Then $E_{\chi_0}$ has dimension one and its line is $i(x_0)$ for a unique $x_0\in X^T(k)$. For any nonzero $e_0\in E_{\chi_0}$, define $f_0\in E^*=\operatorname{Hom}_k(E,k)$ by $f_0(e_0)=1$ and $f_0(E_\chi)=0$ for $\chi\ne\chi_0$. The open subscheme $U=i^{-1}(D(f_0))$, where $D(f_0)$ parametrizes lines on which $f_0$ is nonzero [def-weil-open-immersion], is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $$U(k)=\{y\in X(k):x_0\in\overline{T(k)\cdot y}\}.$$ The closure is in the underlying Zariski space of $X$. The case $r=0$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\dim E=1$ is included.

source.place: Theorem 12.12, printed pp.234--235 (weight decomposition); Lemma 13.51, Proposition 13.52 and Proposition 13.53(a), printed pp.274--276; the coordinate description of the open cell in the proof of Theorem 17.65, printed p.374.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition] to obtain the finite decomposition into nonzero character spaces. Characters of the chosen split torus are Laurent monomials: a character corresponds to a group-like Laurent polynomial, and comparing coefficients in its coproduct forces exactly one monomial, with coefficient one. Thus [lem-sfb-projective-torus-fixed-weight-schemes] applies. It gives a separating cocharacter, and, for any such cocharacter, identifies the fixed subscheme of $X$ for its action with $X^T$. Fix one, write $E_0=E_{\chi_0}$ for its least-weight space and $m_0=m_{\chi_0}$. Also [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] makes $X$ regular and locally Noetherian; [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] then makes the nonempty connected $X$ integral. In particular $|X|$ is irreducible.

source.place: Theorem 12.12, pp.234--235; Lemma 13.51, p.274; Proposition 13.53(a), pp.275--276 (irreducibility input); Stacks Tags 056S (lemma-smooth-regular), 0569 (lemma-regular-normal), 033N (lemma-normal-locally-Noetherian).

proof.text:
Let $W\subseteq X$ be the open set where the projection of the tautological line to $E_0$ is nonzero. Projection defines $p:W\to\mathbf P(E_0)$. Here are the coordinates, including the needed scheme-theoretic factorization. Choose a weight basis; on a chart with a least-weight coordinate $z_i\ne0$, the coordinates of $p$ are $z_j/z_i$ for $e_j\in E_0$, and zero for the other coordinates. They glue, since changing $i$ rescales the same projected vector. For an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of this chart in $W$, the formulas
$$z_j/z_i\longmapsto t^{m_{\chi_j}-m_0}(z_j/z_i)$$
define a morphism $\mathbf A^1_B\to D_+(z_i)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. All exponents are nonnegative; at zero this is $p$. On $t\ne0$ this is the given cocharacter action and lies in $X$. The affine ideal of $X\cap D_+(z_i)$, supplied by [def-weil-closed-immersion], therefore maps to zero in $B[t,t^{-1}]$, hence in $B[t]$, since localization at the indeterminate is injective even when $B$ has zero divisors. Thus the morphism factors through $X$, and so does its value $p$ at zero. A line in $E_0$ is fixed by $T$ after every algebra extension because $T$ acts there by a scalar. The representing property of the given $X^T$ therefore makes $p$ a morphism $W\to X^T$.

source.place: Example 13.50 and Proposition 13.53(a), pp.274--276: minimum-weight limit formula, expanded on standard charts; Stacks Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion), affine ideal description.

proof.text: The spanning hypothesis implies $W\ne\varnothing$: otherwise every line $i(y)$ for $y\in X(k)$ would have zero projection to the nonzero space $E_0$. Being a nonempty open subset of the irreducible $X$, $W$ is irreducible. The continuous image $p(|W|)$ in the finite disjoint union $|X^T|$ is consequently a singleton, say $x_0$. The morphism $p$ factors through that open-and-closed component $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $i(x_0)$ is a line $L\subseteq E_0$. For every $y=[v]\in X(k)$ with $v_0\ne0$, we have $[v_0]=i(x_0)$, so $v_0\in L$; when $v_0=0$ this containment also holds. Project the equality $\operatorname{span}_k\{i(y):y\in X(k)\}=E$ onto $E_0$. Its projected generators all belong to $L$, whence $E_0\subseteq L$. As $L\subseteq E_0$ is nonzero, $E_0=L$ has dimension one. Injectivity of the closed immersion gives uniqueness of $x_0$.

source.place: Proposition 13.53(a), pp.275--276: nondegeneracy and uniqueness of the minimum-weight line; the projection argument expands the uniqueness step without requiring the full Bialynicki--Birula decomposition.

proof.text:
Choose any $e_0\ne0$ in the now one-dimensional $E_0$ and extend it by weight bases of the other summands. Its dual coordinate $z_0$ is precisely the stated $f_0$. Thus $D(f_0)=D_+(z_0)$, which is affine with polynomial coordinates $z_j/z_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. The affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives
$$U=i^{-1}(D(f_0))\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(k[z_j/z_0:j\ne0]/I)$$
for the ideal of the closed subscheme on this chart. Consequently $U$ is affine; moreover $U=W$ because $E_0$ has dimension one.

source.place: Theorem 17.65, p.374, paragraph identifying the open cell by its nonzero minimum-weight coordinate; Stacks Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion), item (2).

proof.text:
For $y=[v]\in U(k)$, rescale $v$ so that $v_0=e_0$. The polynomial curve from step 2 is
$$t\longmapsto[e_0+\sum_{\chi
e\chi_0}t^{m_\chi-m_0}v_\chi]\in U.$$
Its value at zero is $x_0$, and for $t\in k^	imes$ it equals $\lambda(t)y$. Since the algebraically closed field $k$ is infinite, $k^	imes$ is Zariski dense in $\mathbf A^1_k$ (a nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots). Continuity therefore places $x_0$ in $\overline{\lambda(k^	imes)y}\subseteq\overline{T(k)y}$. Conversely, if $y
otin U(k)$, its least-weight component is zero. Every $T(k)$-translate then belongs to the closed hyperplane $\mathbf P( igoplus_{\chi
e\chi_0}E_\chi)$, defined by the coordinate equation $f_0=0$. Its intersection with $X$ is closed and excludes $x_0$, so $x_0
otin\overline{T(k)y}$. This proves exactly the asserted equality. If $r=0$, there is one weight, $W=X$ and $p=i$; the same singleton-image and spanning argument gives $\dim E=1$, and $U=X=\operatorname{Spec}k$ in the stated case. No nontriviality of $\lambda$ was used.

The printed 'dim = 2' in the proof of 13.53(a) is a typo, as the report says. Over algebraically closed k the item's spanning hypothesis is the same as Milne's nondegeneracy, because the span of X is T-stable. Step 1: the weight decomposition and the fixed-weight node supply the separating λ, P(E)^T = ⨿P(E_χ), T-invariant charts and X^T as a fibre product; their Laurent-monomial premise is shown by the group-like coefficient argument. Smooth⇒regular plus regular, connected, nonempty⇒integral gives irreducibility. Step 2: I recomputed the chart action z_j/z_i ↦ t^{m_j−m_0}z_j/z_i. All exponents are ≥0, the ideal dies in B[t,t^-1] and so in B[t] by injectivity, and p lands in X^T scheme-theoretically. Step 3: W is nonempty and irreducible, its image in the finite discrete X^T is one point, and projecting the span gives E_0=L of dimension 1; x_0 is unique since i is injective on k-points. Step 4: U is closed in the chart D_+(z_0), so it is affine (01QO clause of def-weil-closed-immersion). Step 5: the polynomial curve and density of k^× in A^1 give one inclusion; the closed T-stable hyperplane section missing x_0 gives the other. Edge cases checked: P^1 with two weights, Veronese conic with weights 0,1,2, Spec k, r=0. No duplicates: projective-attracting-cells is a different G_m stratification statement.
